hero.headline: Port St. Lucie mayor race heads to November runoff between Shannon Martin and Steven Giordano
hero.teaser: Port St. Lucie Mayor Shannon Martin and challenger Steven Giordano will face off in the November general election after neither candidate secured the 50% threshold needed to win ou
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie Mayor Shannon Martin and challenger Steven Giordano will face off in the November general election after neither candidate secured the 50% threshold needed to win outright in Tuesday's primary race. Martin captured nearly 48% of the vote while Giordano received approximately 35%, forcing a runoff between the top two candidates. Third candidate Eric Strazzeri was eliminated from the race after receiving nearly 17% of the vote.

Both candidates addressed how an ongoing investigation into campaign signs may have affected Tuesday's results. The investigation has been a focal point in the mayoral campaign leading up to the primary. Giordano told WPTV at his election watch party at My Brother's BBQ that if the investigation would have happened earlier, he thinks the results would have swayed better to his race. Martin acknowledged the investigation's potential impact during a phone interview with WPTV, saying she thinks that had something to do with it but plans to keep focused on the issues important to residents.

Martin said she plans to let her track record with the city speak to voters as the campaign moves forward. The incumbent emphasized her experience leading the city and her commitment to continuing her work for residents. Giordano outlined his campaign priorities for the November race, focusing on supporting local youth programs and local businesses. Giordano said he is the people's mayor and the people's voice and is very excited to be in this position.

The November general election will determine who leads Port St. Lucie for the next four years. Voters will choose between Martin's experience as the current mayor and Giordano's vision for change in city leadership. Family and friends gathered at Giordano's election watch party to celebrate advancing to the general election.

cards.headline: Miami woman arrested in Martin County for posing as bank representative, hiding stolen cash in body
cards.teaser: A Miami woman was arrested in Martin County after allegedly posing as a bank representative to scam residents out of thousands of dollars, according to Martin County Sheriff John B
cards.body:
A Miami woman was arrested in Martin County after allegedly posing as a bank representative to scam residents out of thousands of dollars, according to Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek. Monquie Love Turnbull, 32, drove from Miami to Martin County where she approached two residents, claiming their debit cards were compromised and needed to be turned in for replacement. One victim lost $3,180 from her account minutes after Turnbull left with the card.

Deputies located Turnbull on Bridge Road in Hobe Sound near the I-95 interchange and conducted a traffic stop. Aerial footage shows sheriff's deputies following Turnbull on I-95 before stopping her vehicle. The first victim was brought to the scene and positively identified Turnbull as the woman who had collected her card. A search of the vehicle turned up a surgical mask and multiple yellow envelopes matching witness descriptions.

Turnbull never mentioned she was carrying $3,180 in cash concealed in her body when she was arrested, and the money was not discovered until she was being processed into the jail. She revealed she had the money inside her body when she complained of pain during a jail phone call to an unknown man. The sheriff's office confirmed the cash is the same money taken from one of her alleged scam victims. Budensiek said the victim handed over all her rent money to the scammer.

The case began Monday when Turnbull, using the alias Monica, arrived at an elderly victim's home after an unidentified male caller posing as a Chase Bank fraud representative told the victim her account had been compromised. Turnbull verified herself with a code relayed from the caller and collected the card, cutting it in half in front of the victim and placing the pieces in a manila envelope. While deputies were investigating that report, they received a second call identifying Turnbull as a possible suspect in a nearly identical incident targeting another victim the same day. Turnbull now faces charges including scheme to defraud, grand theft, fraudulent use of a credit or debit card without consent involving a victim 60 or older, fraudulent use of ID without consent, felony use of a two-way communication device to facilitate a felony, and introducing contraband into a corrections facility. She is being held on a $500,000 bond.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County Clerk Michael Caruso extradited to Orange County jail on five felony child sex abuse charges
cards.teaser: Suspended Palm Beach County Clerk of Court Michael Caruso was extradited to Orange County jail Wednesday after his arrest on five felony child sex abuse charges. Caruso, 67, faces
cards.body:
Suspended Palm Beach County Clerk of Court Michael Caruso was extradited to Orange County jail Wednesday after his arrest on five felony child sex abuse charges. Caruso, 67, faces charges of kidnapping, lewd or lascivious molestation, lewd or lascivious exhibition, luring or enticing a child, and child abuse causing mental injury, according to the arrest warrant and affidavit filed in Orange County Circuit Court. Gov. Ron DeSantis immediately suspended Caruso from office following his arrest Tuesday.

Caruso made his first appearance Wednesday morning at the Palm Beach County Criminal Justice Complex, where a judge issued a comprehensive no-contact order prohibiting any contact with the alleged victim, immediate family, witnesses, and any individual under the age of 18. When Caruso's defense attorney requested an extradition bond that would allow him to remain out of jail while awaiting transport, the judge denied the request, stating it was inappropriate based upon the nature and extent of the charges. The judge clarified that the Palm Beach County court was not making any probable cause findings, but was only facilitating Caruso's expedited transfer to Orange County, where the charges originated.

According to court documents, the charges stem from allegations involving multiple incidents with a child victim spanning nearly a year, including incidents during a family cruise in August 2025. The victim disclosed the abuse during a recorded interview with Orange County law enforcement and has been receiving therapeutic services since April 2026. When confronted by family members in December 2025, court documents state Caruso made partial admissions while making threatening statements about potential consequences if the allegations were reported.

Shannon Ramsey-Chessman, the chief of staff and chief deputy clerk, has been appointed as interim clerk following Caruso's suspension. The Florida Department of Law Enforcement is overseeing the transition and ensuring no files or records are removed from the clerk's office. Questions remain about Caruso's status on the November ballot, where he was scheduled to face Democrat Yvette Drucker for the clerk position. The Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections is awaiting guidance from state officials on how to proceed with his candidacy.

cards.headline: Miami woman accused of scamming Martin County seniors hid $3,200 in her body during jail intake
cards.teaser: A 32-year-old Miami woman arrested in Martin County for posing as a bank representative to scam seniors faces an additional charge after deputies say she smuggled $3,180 in cash in
cards.body:
A 32-year-old Miami woman arrested in Martin County for posing as a bank representative to scam seniors faces an additional charge after deputies say she smuggled $3,180 in cash into jail concealed in her body. Monquie Love Turnbull never mentioned she was carrying the money when arrested, and it was not discovered until she was being processed into the Martin County jail. The Martin County Sheriff's Office confirmed the cash is the same money taken from one of her alleged victims.

The case began Monday when Turnbull showed up at an elderly victim's home in Martin County claiming the person's bank account had been compromised. Investigators say an unidentified male caller, posing as a Chase Bank fraud representative, told the victim her account had been compromised and that someone would come to her home to collect and destroy her card before a replacement arrived. Turnbull, using the alias Monica, arrived at the home, verified herself with a code relayed from the caller, and collected the card, cutting it in half in front of the victim and placing the pieces in a manila envelope. Minutes later, the victim's bank account was drained through a $3,000 withdrawal and a $180 ATM withdrawal.

Sheriff John Budensiek said Turnbull revealed she had the money inside her body when she complained of pain during a jail phone call to an unknown man. Deputies went back to the jail and interviewed her, and she admitted to having money inside of her. While deputies were investigating the first report, they were alerted to a second call identifying Turnbull as a possible suspect in a nearly identical incident targeting another victim the same day. That attempt was caught on a Ring doorbell camera, but the second victim's family member grew skeptical and refused to hand over the card.

Deputies located Turnbull's vehicle, a gray two-door Nissan Altima, on Bridge Road in Hobe Sound near the I-95 interchange and conducted a traffic stop. The first victim was brought to the scene and positively identified Turnbull as Monica from about 15 feet away. Turnbull now faces a charge of introducing contraband into a corrections facility on top of her original charges including scheme to defraud, grand theft, fraudulent use of a credit or debit card without consent involving a victim 60 or older, fraudulent use of ID without consent, and felony use of a two-way communication device to facilitate a felony. She is being held on a $500,000 bond.

cards.headline: Indian River County school superintendent Dr. Moore to step down June 2027
cards.teaser: School District of Indian River County Superintendent Dr. Moore announced Wednesday he will conclude his tenure with the district effective June 30, 2027, after nearly seven years
cards.body:
School District of Indian River County Superintendent Dr. Moore announced Wednesday he will conclude his tenure with the district effective June 30, 2027, after nearly seven years of service. Moore shared his decision with school board members and his Cabinet Leadership Team before informing district and school leaders and broader SDIRC staff. His tenure currently ranks as the second longest among Florida's appointed district school superintendents.

Moore said during his time leading the district, SDIRC advanced from 38th to 5th among Florida's 67 school districts based on District Grade, earned 4 consecutive A district grades, and grew the share of schools earning an A or B from 47 percent to 100 percent. The district also achieved a 96 percent high school graduation rate and was named the No. 1 Best Place to Teach in Florida by Niche for 2026. Moore was named the 2025 Florida Superintendent of the Year and a national finalist.

As Moore enters his final school year, he identified two priorities: ensuring every SDIRC school earns an A grade and positioning the district to become the No. 1 school district in Florida. Moore said the district has spent close to seven years proving that dramatic improvement is possible, and this year he wants the district to demonstrate how far a mature, coherent, high-performing system can go.

Following his departure, Moore said he intends to explore opportunities to help other leaders and school systems create conditions for exceptional student outcomes. Moore said serving as Superintendent of Schools has been one of the greatest privileges of his professional life, and his belief in the power of public education to transform lives is stronger than ever.

cards.headline: Florida school bus and speed zone camera lawsuits face dismissals and legal setbacks
cards.teaser: Legal challenges to automated school bus and school zone cameras generating millions of citations across Florida are hitting roadblocks, with judges dismissing cases and ruling against drivers who contest tickets.
cards.body:
Miami-based Attorney Gino Moreno filed three lawsuits last year after drivers hit with $225 school bus camera fines had no way to challenge their fines because the cameras started rolling without the proper due process in place. His cases have since hit a wall. In Polk County, a judge dismissed his federal case. In Miami-Dade, a revised complaint is pending, and in Hillsborough County, his client Stanley Shultz is still waiting to see if his case will move forward.

Shultz, who lives in Plant City, was fined for illegally passing a school bus even though video from his citation shows the bus's warning lights never flashed. Shultz appealed the fine, but a judge in Tallahassee upheld it, despite state law requiring appeals must be heard by local hearing officers. Attorney Ira Karmelin with The Ticket Clinic has successfully used arguments about unapproved radar devices to get school speed zone tickets thrown out, but judges are now starting to side with the state's claim of exemption.

Since the cameras began operating in Florida, they have generated well over 1 million citations and tens of millions of dollars in paid fines as of earlier this year. Concerns have emerged over school speed zone cameras, with drivers fined when school was not in session or when signs directing them to slow down when flashing never flashed. Questions also emerged about the camera devices themselves, as the radar inside the cameras, which state law requires to be approved by the state, is not approved, though the state maintains it's exempt.

cards.headline: Vero Beach shooting victim identified as Dawn Kriskewic, suspect Matthew Waggle remains at large
cards.teaser: The Indian River County Sheriff's Office identified the woman shot and killed Sunday morning in Vero Beach as 52-year-old Dawn Kriskewic. The Sheriff's Office announced the identif
cards.body:
Kriskewic was found in the 500 block of First Street, just outside Vero Beach, Sunday morning. Deputies performed lifesaving measures before she was taken to a trauma center, where she later died. Investigators delayed releasing her name while they worked to locate and notify several out-of-state next of kin.

Investigators have identified 33-year-old Matthew Waggle as a person of interest in the homicide. He has yet to be located or charged. A nationwide BOLO has been issued for Waggle. Investigators say he should be considered armed and dangerous and should not be approached.

The Sheriff's Office said investigators believe Kriskewic had been trying to end a relationship with Waggle and are investigating the shooting as a domestic violence homicide. The agency has been using its Real Time Crime Center and a network of Flock license plate cameras as investigators search for Waggle and work to piece together what happened.

hero.headline: Kuhio Aloy hits first two pro homers as St. Lucie Mets fall 7-3 to Jupiter
hero.teaser: Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets fell 7-3 to the Jupiter Hammerheads to close out a difficult road series.
hero.body:
Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets could not overcome a late surge by the Jupiter Hammerheads in a 7-3 loss at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

The defeat ended a difficult six-game series for St. Lucie, with Jupiter winning five of the six games. The Mets have now lost seven of their last eight.

Aloy, the Mets' 11th-round pick out of Arkansas, provided the offensive highlight for St. Lucie with a pair of solo home runs.

His first came in the second inning and gave the Mets a 1-0 lead. Aloy went deep again in the sixth, tying the game 2-2.

Jupiter slugger Echedry Vargas answered with another big performance of his own. Vargas hit a two-run homer off Candido Cuevas in the fourth inning to put the Hammerheads ahead 2-1.

After Aloy tied the game in the top of the sixth, Vargas responded in the bottom half with a towering solo home run off Conner Ware, putting Jupiter back in front 3-2.

It was Vargas' second multi-homer game of the series. He finished the six-game set with five home runs and now leads the Florida State League with 21 this season. Vargas is the first Hammerheads player to reach at least 20 home runs in a season since Marcell Ozuna in 2012.

Jupiter pulled away with three runs in the seventh inning. One run scored on a groundout and another came home on an error before Jeremy Almonte delivered an RBI double off Jose Guevara, stretching the Hammerheads' lead to 6-2.

The Mets attempted to rally in the ninth after Jupiter reliever Ian Medina walked four batters. Elian Peña drew a bases-loaded walk to force home a run and cut the deficit to 7-3.

Davidxon Lara then entered for Jupiter and retired John Smith III on a groundout with the tying run at the plate to end the game.

Mets starter Will Watson, who is working his way back from an oblique injury on a Minor League Baseball rehab assignment, pitched three scoreless innings.

St. Lucie finished the day at 17-30 in the second half and 50-63 overall.

The Mets are off Monday before returning home Tuesday to begin a six-game series against the Lakeland Flying Tigers at Clover Park in Port St. Lucie. First pitch for Tuesday's opener is scheduled for 6:10 p.m.

hero.headline: Palm Beach County Clerk Michael Caruso extradited to Orange County jail on five felony child sex abuse charges
hero.teaser: Suspended Palm Beach County Clerk of Court Michael Caruso was extradited to Orange County jail Wednesday after his arrest on five felony child sex abuse charges. Caruso, 67, faces
hero.body:
Suspended Palm Beach County Clerk of Court Michael Caruso was extradited to Orange County jail Wednesday after his arrest on five felony child sex abuse charges. Caruso, 67, faces charges of kidnapping, lewd or lascivious molestation, lewd or lascivious exhibition, luring or enticing a child, and child abuse causing mental injury, according to the arrest warrant and affidavit filed in Orange County Circuit Court. Gov. Ron DeSantis immediately suspended Caruso from office following his arrest Tuesday.

Caruso made his first appearance Wednesday morning at the Palm Beach County Criminal Justice Complex, where a judge issued a comprehensive no-contact order prohibiting any contact with the alleged victim, immediate family, witnesses, and any individual under the age of 18. When Caruso's defense attorney requested an extradition bond that would allow him to remain out of jail while awaiting transport, the judge denied the request, stating it was inappropriate based upon the nature and extent of the charges. The judge clarified that the Palm Beach County court was not making any probable cause findings, but was only facilitating Caruso's expedited transfer to Orange County, where the charges originated.

According to court documents, the charges stem from allegations involving multiple incidents with a child victim spanning nearly a year, including incidents during a family cruise in August 2025. The victim disclosed the abuse during a recorded interview with Orange County law enforcement and has been receiving therapeutic services since April 2026. When confronted by family members in December 2025, court documents state Caruso made partial admissions while making threatening statements about potential consequences if the allegations were reported.

Shannon Ramsey-Chessman, the chief of staff and chief deputy clerk, has been appointed as interim clerk following Caruso's suspension. The Florida Department of Law Enforcement is overseeing the transition and ensuring no files or records are removed from the clerk's office. Questions remain about Caruso's status on the November ballot, where he was scheduled to face Democrat Yvette Drucker for the clerk position. The Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections is awaiting guidance from state officials on how to proceed with his candidacy.

cards.headline: Florida school bus and speed zone camera lawsuits face dismissals and legal setbacks
cards.teaser: Legal challenges to automated school bus and school zone cameras generating millions of citations across Florida are hitting roadblocks, with judges dismissing cases and ruling against drivers who contest tickets.
cards.body:
Miami-based Attorney Gino Moreno filed three lawsuits last year after drivers hit with $225 school bus camera fines had no way to challenge their fines because the cameras started rolling without the proper due process in place. His cases have since hit a wall. In Polk County, a judge dismissed his federal case. In Miami-Dade, a revised complaint is pending, and in Hillsborough County, his client Stanley Shultz is still waiting to see if his case will move forward.

Shultz, who lives in Plant City, was fined for illegally passing a school bus even though video from his citation shows the bus's warning lights never flashed. Shultz appealed the fine, but a judge in Tallahassee upheld it, despite state law requiring appeals must be heard by local hearing officers. Attorney Ira Karmelin with The Ticket Clinic has successfully used arguments about unapproved radar devices to get school speed zone tickets thrown out, but judges are now starting to side with the state's claim of exemption.

Since the cameras began operating in Florida, they have generated well over 1 million citations and tens of millions of dollars in paid fines as of earlier this year. Concerns have emerged over school speed zone cameras, with drivers fined when school was not in session or when signs directing them to slow down when flashing never flashed. Questions also emerged about the camera devices themselves, as the radar inside the cameras, which state law requires to be approved by the state, is not approved, though the state maintains it's exempt.

cards.headline: Angie Nixon wins Democratic nomination for Florida U.S. Senate special primary election
cards.teaser: State Rep. Angie Nixon won the Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate in Florida's special primary election Tuesday, defeating Army veteran Alex Vindman.
cards.body:
Vindman gained national attention when he was serving on the National Security Council in 2019, when the Republican president pressured Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to investigate Joe Biden, then a Democratic candidate. He and his brother, Eugene, a lawyer on the National Security Council, reported their concerns and sparked investigations.

Nixon will take on incumbent U.S. Sen. Ashley Moody in the November general election. Moody easily won the GOP primary on Tuesday, defeating three challengers. The winner of November's special election will finish the last two years of Marco Rubio's term after he left the Senate to become U.S. Secretary of State.

A Democrat has not won a Senate seat in Florida since 2012, when former U.S. Sen. Bill Nelson won his third term.

hero.headline: Miami woman accused of scamming Martin County seniors hid $3,200 in her body during jail intake
hero.teaser: A 32-year-old Miami woman arrested in Martin County for posing as a bank representative to scam seniors faces an additional charge after deputies say she smuggled $3,180 in cash in
hero.body:
A 32-year-old Miami woman arrested in Martin County for posing as a bank representative to scam seniors faces an additional charge after deputies say she smuggled $3,180 in cash into jail concealed in her body. Monquie Love Turnbull never mentioned she was carrying the money when arrested, and it was not discovered until she was being processed into the Martin County jail. The Martin County Sheriff's Office confirmed the cash is the same money taken from one of her alleged victims.

The case began Monday when Turnbull showed up at an elderly victim's home in Martin County claiming the person's bank account had been compromised. Investigators say an unidentified male caller, posing as a Chase Bank fraud representative, told the victim her account had been compromised and that someone would come to her home to collect and destroy her card before a replacement arrived. Turnbull, using the alias Monica, arrived at the home, verified herself with a code relayed from the caller, and collected the card, cutting it in half in front of the victim and placing the pieces in a manila envelope. Minutes later, the victim's bank account was drained through a $3,000 withdrawal and a $180 ATM withdrawal.

Sheriff John Budensiek said Turnbull revealed she had the money inside her body when she complained of pain during a jail phone call to an unknown man. Deputies went back to the jail and interviewed her, and she admitted to having money inside of her. While deputies were investigating the first report, they were alerted to a second call identifying Turnbull as a possible suspect in a nearly identical incident targeting another victim the same day. That attempt was caught on a Ring doorbell camera, but the second victim's family member grew skeptical and refused to hand over the card.

Deputies located Turnbull's vehicle, a gray two-door Nissan Altima, on Bridge Road in Hobe Sound near the I-95 interchange and conducted a traffic stop. The first victim was brought to the scene and positively identified Turnbull as Monica from about 15 feet away. Turnbull now faces a charge of introducing contraband into a corrections facility on top of her original charges including scheme to defraud, grand theft, fraudulent use of a credit or debit card without consent involving a victim 60 or older, fraudulent use of ID without consent, and felony use of a two-way communication device to facilitate a felony. She is being held on a $500,000 bond.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie mayor race heads to November runoff between Shannon Martin and Steven Giordano
hero.teaser: Port St. Lucie Mayor Shannon Martin and challenger Steven Giordano will face off in the November general election after neither candidate secured the 50% threshold needed to win ou
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie Mayor Shannon Martin and challenger Steven Giordano will face off in the November general election after neither candidate secured the 50% threshold needed to win outright in Tuesday's primary race. Martin captured nearly 48% of the vote while Giordano received approximately 35%, forcing a runoff between the top two candidates. Third candidate Eric Strazzeri was eliminated from the race after receiving nearly 17% of the vote.

Both candidates addressed how an ongoing investigation into campaign signs may have affected Tuesday's results. The investigation has been a focal point in the mayoral campaign leading up to the primary. Giordano told WPTV at his election watch party at My Brother's BBQ that if the investigation would have happened earlier, he thinks the results would have swayed better to his race. Martin acknowledged the investigation's potential impact during a phone interview with WPTV, saying she thinks that had something to do with it but plans to keep focused on the issues important to residents.

Martin said she plans to let her track record with the city speak to voters as the campaign moves forward. The incumbent emphasized her experience leading the city and her commitment to continuing her work for residents. Giordano outlined his campaign priorities for the November race, focusing on supporting local youth programs and local businesses. Giordano said he is the people's mayor and the people's voice and is very excited to be in this position.

The November general election will determine who leads Port St. Lucie for the next four years. Voters will choose between Martin's experience as the current mayor and Giordano's vision for change in city leadership. Family and friends gathered at Giordano's election watch party to celebrate advancing to the general election.

cards.headline: Bicyclist critically injured in Port St. Lucie crash on Southwest Rosser Boulevard
cards.teaser: A bicyclist was airlifted to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital in critical condition after being struck by a driver with a suspended license Wednesday morning.
cards.body:
A bicyclist is in the hospital after he was struck by a woman who was allegedly driving with a suspended license on Wednesday. According to the Port St. Lucie Police Department, the crash happened around 6:45 a.m. near Southwest Rosser Boulevard and Southwest Meridian Avenue. Police said the bicyclist was riding on Southwest Rosser Boulevard when the crash occurred.

Officers said the bicyclist was breathing but unconscious and was wearing a helmet. He was airlifted to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where he was listed in critical but stable condition and is expected to survive. The driver remained at the scene and was issued a notice to appear after officers determined she was driving with a suspended license. Her vehicle was later removed from the scene by her husband.

Traffic in both directions was shut down, with motorists diverted onto side streets. The investigation remains ongoing.

hero.headline: Vero Beach shooting victim identified as Dawn Kriskewic, suspect Matthew Waggle remains at large
hero.teaser: The Indian River County Sheriff's Office identified the woman shot and killed Sunday morning in Vero Beach as 52-year-old Dawn Kriskewic. The Sheriff's Office announced the identif
hero.body:
The woman found shot in the 500 block of First Street in Vero Beach on Sunday morning has been identified as 52-year-old Dawn Kriskewic, the Indian River County Sheriff's Office confirmed Tuesday. Kriskewic was found in a roadway at 501 First Street on Sunday, Aug. 16, by Indian River County Sheriff's Office deputies. She suffered an apparent gunshot wound. Deputies began life-saving measures on Kriskewic. She was transported to a local hospital, where she was pronounced dead. Investigators delayed releasing her name while they worked to locate and notify several out-of-state next of kin.

The sheriff's office named 33-year-old Matthew Allen Waggle as a person of interest. The sheriff's office said Kriskewic and Waggle were in some sort of a relationship. Investigators believe Kriskewic had been trying to end a relationship with Waggle and are investigating the shooting as a domestic violence homicide. A nationwide BOLO has been issued for Waggle. Investigators say he should be considered armed and dangerous and should not be approached.

As of Tuesday afternoon, law enforcement continues its investigation and search for Waggle. The Sheriff's Office has been using its Real Time Crime Center and a network of Flock license plate cameras as investigators search for Waggle and work to piece together what happened. Anyone with information about the case or Waggle's whereabouts is asked to contact the Indian River County Sheriff's Office or submit information anonymously to Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers.

cards.headline: Former Vero Beach Eagles secretary accused of spending $419,000 on guns, liquor, LEGOs
cards.teaser: Robert John Davison allegedly used nearly $419,000 of Fraternal Order of Eagles funds for personal expenses including firearms, DUI fees, and items for his personal LEGO business.
cards.body:
Robert John Davison served as secretary of Aerie 4374 Fraternal Order of Eagles in Vero Beach from February 2015 until November 2024, when he stopped showing up. The investigation began after a representative was sent to the chapter by the Grand Aerie to examine why membership and the organization's finances were declining. After reviewing expenses, he told deputies that he discovered that Davison had been using the organization's debit card for personal purchases that had not been authorized.

The organization later hired forensic accounting firm Clay Price & Associates, P.A., to review its financial records. On Feb. 24, 2025, the firm reported that Davison had used $418,899.26 in organization funds for personal expenses dating back to 2017. The alleged spending included $115,087.49 in ATM withdrawals and associated fees that investigators say were outside the secretary's authorized duties, $55,175.40 on personal bills including credit cards, vehicle payments, utilities and cellphone bills, $35,094.53 in personal grocery and liquor store purchases, $16,038.66 in unauthorized flights and lodging, $9,861.27 in transfers to Davison's personal Cash App account, $8,791.14 on firearms, ammunition, personal purchases and an NRA membership, $5,930.98 in rideshare expenses, $4,463.52 in personal court payments including child support and DUI-related fees, and at least $2,461.37 in purchases for Davison's personal LEGO business.

The current trustee chairman and the current secretary reportedly verified that the debit card charges were outside Davison's duties and were not authorized by the organization. Davison is accused of embezzlement involving a value of $100,000 or more.
